newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo-Wellcome sales in 4 mths 2.75bln stg.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo-Wellcome sales in 4 mths 2.75bln stg.

text.p: British drugs and pharmaceuticals giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Monday that its sales in the first four months to April 30, 1997 stood at 2.75 billion pounds ($4.5 billion) which was 10 percent higher at constant exchange rate terms than in the same period last year.

Colin Corness, the group chairman, told shareholders at the annual meeting that if exchange rates were to remain at their present level for the rest of 1997, the adverse impact on earnings for the whole year would be around five percent.

"The expected decline in Zantac (ulcer treatment) continues, with sales in the period to April 30 seven percent lower in constant exchange rate terms than the same period last year," Corness told shareholders.

Addressing the same meeting, Richard Sykes, the deputy chairman and chief executive of the group said the company was likely to lose as much as 80 to 90 percent of U.S. sales of Zantac following the expiry of its patent.
Corness said sales of all other group products had increased by 15 percent on the same basis.
"Respiratory products have now become the group's largest therapy area, with sales of antiviral and central nervous system products showing strong growth," he said.
